title: Correctness Checking of MPI+OpenMP Applications Using Vector Clocks in MUST
problem: Hybrid MPI+OpenMP programs can invoke concurrent MPI calls from different threads within the same process, causing correctness errors. Existing correctness tools focus on single programming models and provide limited support for detecting these hybrid application errors.
motivation: Ensuring correctness in hybrid MPI+OpenMP programs is critical for HPC, as combining both models significantly increases complexity and error-proneness.
method: The paper adds vector clocks—a technique that records the order of operations across parallel threads—to the MUST MPI correctness tool to track how OpenMP threads (code segments running simultaneously within the same program) synchronize with each other. It pulls synchronization information from the Archer race detector to understand thread interactions, then uses this data to identify four specific types of errors that occur when multiple threads attempt to make concurrent MPI calls (network communication requests) at the same time.
key_novelty: The innovation is using vector clocks to track OpenMP thread synchronization for detecting errors that occur when multiple threads invoke MPI calls concurrently in the same program.
contributions: Classification of four classes of MPI+OpenMP errors from concurrent MPI calls across different threads
Vector clock-based method for tracking OpenMP thread synchronization to detect hybrid programming errors
Integration of clock-based checks into MUST using Archer's OpenMP synchronization data
Evaluation demonstrating significantly improved error detection on hybrid test cases
limitations: Specific performance overhead, scalability constraints, and generalization beyond provided test suites are not discussed.
